claims.text: Anamae are spirits bound to a single Garou, such as the Heart Guides the Unicorn grants every Garou and the Moonshadows that watch over them for Luna.
Most Garou never learn these spirits exist, but one who builds a bond with an anama gains a spirit that warns, advises, teaches and may fight beside the Garou.

title: Pacts with spirits
summary: How Garou bargain with spirits and what follows a breach.

claims.text: A personal pact binds only one Garou and one spirit and works best as years of mutual trust and respect.
When a Garou does not know the right chiminage, it is wise to ask the spirit honestly what it wants; lying to spirits is always dangerous.
A wronged spirit usually turns hostile and warns its brood, but most forgive a breach given a good reason and chiminage.
A Garou who cannot keep a promise should tell the spirit early, since it may accept another task instead.

title: Englings
summary: Spirits sent by Gaia to be consumed.

claims.text: Englings are spirits Gaia sends to restore the spiritual strength of Gaia’s children; when one dies it gives its Gnosis to those who slew it, and it dies gladly.
Some Incarna have Gafflings that serve the same purpose as physical or spiritual food.
It is proper to thank Gaia and the Engling for the sacrifice, and no individual Engling is named in the Silver Record.

title: The Weaver and Naming
summary: A Garou view of science and the Weaver.

claims.text: Garou elders call science a work of the Weaver and the worst kind of Naming.
In the tale, Gaia granted the Weaver the power of Naming, but the spider abused it, giving things grander names with less meaning until whatever it named grew rigid and dead.
Naming was meant to give life order and renew the Cycle, not to halt it.

title: The broods of the totems
summary: How spirits gather under the great Incarna.

claims.text: The Umbra is dangerous for a lone Gaffling or Jaggling, so while many spirits stay unaligned, many seek an Incarna’s patronage.
Even lesser Incarna ally with stronger spirits, which is how the great Tribal Totems gathered many followers over the ages.
Each great totem is served by a brood, from mighty Jagglings and lesser Incarna to Gafflings spawned from the totem itself.
Garou reach their ancestors through the Past Life Background, and can also meet them in their abodes in the Umbra, some of whose locations are closely kept secrets.
After the Rite of Passage, new Garou are often sent to study under an Ancestor-spirit, learning the past and the Gifts it can teach.
